title: Curiosity may be what drives our brains to become so complex | New Scientist
description: We often think that our ability to be curious stems from our complex, human brain – but what if curiosity shapes that complexity?
author: Jo Marchant

title: Fish pay attention to one influential neighbour in virtual reality | New Scientist
description: Observing interactions between real and virtual rummy-nose tetra fish shows that, within a group, each individual takes cues from only one influential neighbour
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Allergic reactions after sex should be listed as an antibiotic risk, experts say | New Scientist
description: A woman developed a severe allergic reaction to an antibiotic in her partner's semen after sex, prompting clinicians to call for this risk to be listed on the drug's patient information leaflet
author: Carissa Wong

title: Rusty crust made Mars warm and wet | New Scientist
description: It's unclear how and why Mars once became warm enough to allow water to flow on its surface, but a new idea suggests it comes down to rust below the surface
author: Bas den Hond

title: Binance: How did the biggest crypto heist in history just happen? | New Scientist
description: Billions of dollars' worth of cryptocurrency have been stolen in just a matter of minutes. Researchers are already unpicking what went wrong
author: Chris Stokel-Walker

title: Scientists confirm fruit and vegetable skin really is good for you | New Scientist
description: Parts of plants that are usually wasted, from kiwi skin to squash seeds, contain more fibre than the parts of the plant we do eat
author: Madeleine Cuff
